seen_animation: a.png 1-3: a closed book seen at a diagonal, its cover a rectangle with four short dash marks, the spine as a double line on the left edge, a page edge showing on the right, and a drawn hand (finger loops) at the bottom edge. A grey paper outline sits at top left. 4: the cover's lower edge lifts and the hand moves up onto the cover. 5: the cover swings up toward the top right, hinged on the left spine, with the hand on it; the page underneath shows its own dash marks. 6: the cover is nearly edge-on along the spine with the hand gripping it. 7: the hand is at top left holding the cover, which is now a vertical line on the left with loose dashes; the right page is open. 8: the hand is mostly out of frame at top left; a left page outline appears. 9-16: an open book held still, two pages split by a double-line spine, dash marks on both pages, no hand.
seen_film: d.png 1-3: a black binder labelled Federal Reserve Regulations lies closed on a desk; a hand with red nails holds its lower right edge. 4: the hand slides to the right edge and starts lifting the cover. 5: the cover swings up and to the left, blurred, the hand under it; white pages show beneath. 6: the cover is nearly vertical at top left and the hand pushes it over; the text page fills the lower right. 7-8: the hand at top left flips a bundle of pages up and over; the open pages lie in the centre. 9: the hand leaves at top left, and the lifted pages stand up on the left. 10-16: the binder lies open, with a page stack curving up on the left and a text page across the centre; the pages settle with small movements and the camera holds.
named_subject: A ring binder or book (the regulations binder) being opened by a hand; the character is the book with its dash-mark text lines.
evidence: Timing is close. In e.png the cover starts lifting at 6 and in f.png at 7. The cover is edge-on at 9 in e.png and at 9-10 in f.png. The book is open and holding by 14 in e.png and by 15-16 in f.png. The open book in e.png 14-26 matches the doodle (double-line spine, dash lines on both pages) and the film's diagonal layout. The breaks are these. e.png 1-5: the hand stays at the bottom edge and does not move while the film hand slides from bottom centre to the right edge (f.png 1-6). e.png 5 to 6: the cover outline is redrawn as a skewed quadrilateral, and a second page outline pops out on the right side. e.png 6 to 7 to 8: the hand jumps from the bottom edge to mid-cover to the upper left, a large step each frame, and in 7 the cover outline and the page outline overlap (doubling). e.png 9 to 10: the cover goes from an edge-on sliver at the spine to a short slanted stroke on the left, and the hand jumps to the left. e.png 10 to 11: the hand doubles in size and moves to the top-left corner; the left page has no outline, only loose dashes and one vertical line. e.png 12 to 13: the hand disappears in one frame and the full left-page outline pops in, while in f.png the hand is still visible at top left through frame 14. g.png shows the path stepping 1/4 to 7 to 10 to 13 and then jumping back to the centre at 16, which comes from the left page appearing all at once.
primary_gap: The cover-flip and page-turn (e.png 6-13) are drawn as a few disconnected poses: the hand jumps between positions and changes size, the cover outline is redrawn instead of rotating about the spine, and the left page and hand swap in and out in single frames.
closes_when: Each frame from 6 to 14 shows the same cover rectangle rotating about the fixed spine line by a small, even angle, the hand stays a constant size and travels with the cover's free edge, and the left page outline grows out of the rotating cover so that the hand exits at 14-15 instead of vanishing at 13.
protect: The doodle's construction: the double-line spine, short slanted dash marks as text, and the plain single-stroke page outlines. The diagonal layout matching the film's open binder. The overall timing (closed through about frame 5, flip at 6-12, held open from 14). The steady hold in e.png 14-26.
identity_gap: The open book in the held frames reads as c.png rotated, but in frames 11-12 the left page loses its outline and becomes floating dashes, which the doodle never does.
